# unfirehose — LLM & Agent API Reference

> Base URL: http://localhost:3000 (self-hosted)
> All endpoints return JSON unless noted (SSE streams, NDJSON, raw blobs). Errors: `{ error, detail?, status? }`
> No authentication required for local instance.
> Every `METHOD /api/path` heading below matches a route file under `apps/web/src/app/api`; `src/app/llms-txt.test.ts` fails when one is added or removed without updating this file.

## Logs & Thinking Traces

### GET /api/logs
Search all conversation logs across harnesses (Claude Code, Fetch, uncloseai). Newest first.
- `?search=error` — substring match over every content block (text, reasoning, tool input and tool result)
- `?project=-home-fox-git-myapp` — filter by project
- `?types=user,assistant,system` — filter message types (default: all three)
- `?has_thinking=true` — only messages carrying a non-empty reasoning/thinking block; this is how to find thinking traces
- `?from=2026-03-01&to=2026-03-07` — date range; a bare date for `to` covers that whole day
- `?session=abc123` — single session uuid
- `?sidechain=true|false|all` — subagent filter; `true` = only subagent (Task-spawned) messages, `false` = only top-level, `all` (default) = both
- `?limit=100&offset=0` — pagination (default 100, max 500)
→ `{ entries: [{ id, type, subtype, timestamp, model, sessionUuid, sessionDisplay, projectName, projectDisplay, preview, kind, tool, toolArg, isError, hasReasoning, durationMs, inputTokens, outputTokens, isSidechain }], total, limit, offset }`

### GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}
Full conversation replay for a session, as canonical unfirehose/1.0 messages read from its JSONL on disk (thinking blocks included).
- `?project=-home-fox-git-myapp` — required; picks the harness adapter and the file
- `?types=user,assistant` — filter canonical roles (`user`, `assistant`, `system`, `tool`); default all
- `?offset=0&limit=500` — paginate messages (default limit 500)
- `?stream=true` — NDJSON stream (`application/x-ndjson`, one message per line) instead of JSON
→ `{ entries: [...], count, offset, limit }`; 400 without `project`, 404 when the file is gone

### GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/chain
Provenance verdict for one session as the ingester recorded it — `unchained` / `open` / `verified` / `corrupted` — with the first break's index and reason, and the root the closed record committed to.
- `?project=...&live=1` — re-read the journal from disk and verify it now (`live=1` needs `project`); a trailing partial line is reported as `partialTail`, never counted as a break
- `events` — every finding for the session by line index, oldest line first (up to 200): each leaf the witness saw differ (`rewritten`; `hash_mismatch` when a chained line's bytes changed under its own hash), each range of lines the file lost (`lost`, `seq`..`seq_to`), each chain break the verifier hit by reason. One row per finding, never one per session.
- `lanes` — the closed record's lane heads checked against lane files on disk: `{ total, anchored, unanchored, uncheckable, checkedAt }`, or null when no lanes were named
- `closeReason` — set only when a session closed abnormally
→ `{ sessionId, state, recorded: {...} | null, events: [{ id, seq, seq_to, kind, recorded_hash, current_hash, current_text, observed_at }], lanes, closeReason, live?: { state, breaks, ..., partialTail, path } }`

### GET /api/sessions/anchor-events
Every tamper finding across every session, newest first — the feed behind the per-session `events`. A session with two edits is two rows; a re-audit that finds the same two again adds none; a line edited a second time is a new row because its current hash is new.
- `?hours=24` — window (max 1 year)
- `?limit=100` — rows, newest first (max 1000)
- `?kind=rewritten|hash_mismatch|lost|prev_mismatch|root_mismatch|…` — one finding kind
→ `{ hours, events: [{ id, session_uuid, project, harness, seq, seq_to, kind, recorded_hash, current_hash, current_text, observed_at }] }`

### GET /api/sessions/chains
Chain verdict and witness state for many sessions in one call — what a list view shows beside each id. A session the ingester has not recorded yet is absent.
- `?ids=a,b,c` — session uuids, up to 2000
→ `{ chains: { [uuid]: { state, anchor: intact|rewritten|missing|null, breaks, firstBreak } } }`

### GET /api/sessions/rewrites
Harnesses caught in the act. The witness records an unchained journal (Claude Code, Codex, hermes-agent…) only once its file has been quiet ten minutes, because such a writer rewrites lines near the tail of a live transcript. This endpoint is the diagnostic on the other side of that gate: a live shadow of every line, and a row for each line that came back different — before and after text and hash, how far from the tail it sat, and which JSON keys moved (`message.usage` is a refresh, `message.content` an edit). `truncated` rows are lines the file lost.
- `?hours=24` — window for both summary and rows
- `?limit=50` — rows, newest first (max 1000)
- `?session=<uuid>` / `?harness=claude-code` — narrow the rows
→ `{ summary: { total, sessions, byHarness, maxTailDistance, contentChanged, metadataOnly, truncations, byChangedKey }, rows: [{ id, session_uuid, project, harness, seq, kind: rewritten|truncated, observed_at, file_lines, tail_distance, before_hash, after_hash, before_text, after_text, before_len, after_len, truncated, changed_keys: [...], content_changed, before_type, after_type }] }`

### GET /api/session/tail
SSE tail of one session JSONL, rendered as compact readable lines (role, text, tools, reasoning). Polls every 1.5 s locally, 4 s over SSH.
- `?path=/home/fox/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl` — required; must be a `.jsonl` under a `~/.<harness>/projects/` or `~/.<harness>/unfirehose/` directory
- `?host=cammy` — read it on a mesh node over SSH (default localhost)
- `?lines=40` — entries to show (5–200)
→ SSE: `{ type: "tail", content }` whenever a tail changes

### GET /api/tool-results
Archived tool-result spill files. Claude Code writes large tool outputs to
`~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/` and keeps only the path
in the transcript, then deletes those files once they pass `cleanupPeriodDays`
(30 days by default). Ingest copies the bytes into our content-addressed blob
store, so a transcript reference stays resolvable after the sweep.
- `?session=<uuid>` — every spill for one session
- `?tool_use_id=toolu_...` — resolve a specific reference seen in a transcript
- `?limit=100` — max 1000
→ `{ count, results: [{ sessionUuid, toolUseId, relPath, mimeType, sizeBytes, hash, archivedAt, url }] }`

Nested spills keep their subdirectory in `relPath` — a single PDF read lands as
`pdf-<uuid>/page-NN.jpg`, so many rows share one `toolUseId`.

### GET /api/tool-results/{hash}
Serve an archived payload by sha256, with its recorded mime type.
→ raw bytes, or 404 once the blob is gone, 400 for a malformed hash


## Todo System

### GET /api/todos
All todos with filters, grouped for a kanban board. Deleted todos are never returned.
- `?project=...` — one project (encoded name)
- `?status=pending,in_progress` — comma-separated statuses
- `?source=claude` — one source (claude, fetch, manual, …)
- `?completedDays=7` — how many days of completed todos to keep (0–365)
- `?limit=400` — default 400 unscoped, 2000 with `project` (max 2000)
→ `{ todos: [...], byProject: [{ project, display, projectPath, todos: [...] }], limit, truncated, counts: { pending, inProgress, completed, total } }`

### POST /api/todos
Create a todo. With no project given, it lands on the session's project, else on our first project.
← `{ content: "Fix the thing", source?: "manual", projectId?: 12, projectName?: "-home-fox-git-myapp", sessionUuid?: "...", status?: "pending" | "in_progress" }`
→ `{ ok: true, id: 123, uuid }`

### PATCH /api/todos
Update a single todo. Terminal statuses (`completed`, `obsolete`, `deleted`) are recorded to our triage file so they survive a database rebuild; completing a todo culls a deployment whose todos are all done.
← `{ id: 123, status?: "completed", estimatedMinutes?: 30, content?: "..." }`
→ `{ ok: true }`

### DELETE /api/todos
Soft-delete todos (status `deleted`, kept for history).
← `{ id: 123 }` or `{ ids: [1,2,3] }` (max 500)
→ `{ ok: true, deleted: 3 }`

### GET /api/todos/{id}
One todo with everything around it: project, originating session, recent project sessions, attachments, deployment history, session token usage, and the todos it is blocked by.
→ `{ id, uuid, content, status, activeForm, source, externalId, estimatedMinutes, blockedBy, createdAt, updatedAt, completedAt, project: { name, display, path }, session, recentSessions: [...], attachments: [...], deployments: [...], sessionTokens, blockedByTodos: [...] }`

### GET /api/todos/pending
Actionable todos (pending + in_progress) as a flat array, in progress first.
- `?project=-home-fox-git-myapp` — by project
- `?source=claude` — by source
- `?search=auth` — search content
- `?quick=true` — 15 minutes or under, or not yet estimated
- `?needs_ticket=true` — estimated over 15 minutes
- `?limit=100` — default 100, max 1000
→ `[{ id, uuid, content, status, source, externalId, estimatedMinutes, activeForm, blockedBy, project, projectDisplay, sessionUuid, sessionDisplay, createdAt, updatedAt, needsTicket, staleDays }]`

### GET /api/todos/summary
Landscape overview — counts, stale items, by-project breakdown.
→ `{ counts: { pending, inProgress, completed, total }, totalMinutes, unestimated, needsTicket, staleCount, byProject: [...], bySource: [...], oldestPending: {...} | null }`

### GET /api/todos/stale
Open todos not touched in N days.
- `?days=3` — threshold (default 3)
- `?limit=50` — default 50, max 500
- `?project=...`
→ `{ staleThresholdDays, count, todos: [...] }`

### GET /api/todos/triage
Open todos for one project grouped by originating session, stalest session first — the BLACKOPS triage view: read a session's mission (`firstPrompt`) and age, then trash the batch or keep items.
- `?project=...` — required
- `?status=pending,in_progress` — default
- `?limit=20` — max sessions (max 100)
→ `{ project, sessionCount, todoCount, sessions: [{ sessionUuid, sessionDisplay, firstPrompt, sessionCreated, sessionUpdated, staleDays, todos: [...] }] }`

### PATCH /api/todos/bulk
Bulk update multiple todos (max 500).
← `{ ids: [1,2,3], status?: "completed", estimatedMinutes?: 30 }`
→ `{ ok: true, updated: 3 }`

### GET /api/todos/graph
Graphviz visualization of todo dependencies (`blocked_by`).
- `?project=...&status=pending,in_progress`
- `?layout=LR` — left-to-right; anything else is top-to-bottom (`TB`)
→ `{ svg, nodeCount, edgeCount, dot }`

### GET /api/todos/attachments
List a todo's attachments, newest first.
- `?todoId=123` — required
→ `{ attachments: [{ id, todoId, filename, mimeType, sizeBytes, hash, createdAt }] }`

### POST /api/todos/attachments
Attach files to a todo. `multipart/form-data` with `todoId` and one or more `files` (max 10 MB each). Stored content-addressed at `~/.unfirehose/attachments/{sha256}`.
→ `{ ok: true, attachments: [...] }`

### DELETE /api/todos/attachments
Remove one attachment; the blob goes too once nothing else references its hash.
← `{ id: 456 }`
→ `{ ok: true }`

### GET /api/todos/attachments/{hash}
Serve an attachment by sha256 with its recorded mime type and filename.
→ raw bytes, or 404 / 400 for a malformed hash

### POST /api/sessions/{sessionId}/inject
Write a `TodoWrite` tool call into a session's JSONL, so the todos arrive as native tool calls on the next ingest.
← `{ todos: [{ content: "Fix auth", status?: "pending" }] }`
→ `{ ok: true, injected, ids, file }`


## Projects

### GET /api/projects
List all projects, served from the list our worker keeps; `X-Computed-At` says how old it is.
→ `[{ name, displayName, path, sessionCount, totalMessages, tokens: { input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite }, latestActivity, hasMemory, harnesses, foldedCount }]`

### GET /api/projects/activity
Activity metrics across projects, with a cost estimate per project.
- `?days=30` — lookback period
- `?project=...` — single project with recent prompts matched to commits and git context
→ `[{ name, user_messages, assistant_messages, thinking_blocks, ..., cost_estimate, market_estimate, avoided_estimate }]` or, with `project`, `{ project, recentPrompts, git: { isDirty, unpushedCount, remoteUrl } | null }`

### GET /api/projects/git-status
Dirty and unpushed counts for every project repo, keyed by project. Answers at once from what our background sweep has gathered so far; `X-Sweep-Complete: true` once a sweep has finished.
→ `{ [project]: { dirty, unpushed, branch } }`

### GET /api/projects/metadata
Repo facts for one project (cached 60 s).
- `?project=...` — required
→ `{ repoPath, branch, remotes: [...], recentCommits: [...], claudeMd, claudeMdExists }`

### GET /api/projects/merge
Groups of project rows that share git identity (root commit + origin) within one harness slot — what the next ingest would auto-merge.
→ `{ groupCount, groups: [[{ prefix, root, origin, id, name, display_name, path, last_cwd_seen }]] }`

### POST /api/projects/merge
Merge one project row into another, or sweep every identity group.
← `{ sourceId: 97, targetId: 106 }` — source is dropped; target absorbs sessions, todos, usage, deployments, alerts and agent actions; source's name becomes an alias
← `{ autoIdentity: true }` — merge every group into its most recently active member (idempotent)
→ `{ merged: 1, sourceId, targetId }` or `{ merged }`

### GET /api/projects/{project}/full
Everything about one project in one call.
→ `{ visibility, project: { name, displayName, path, firstSeen }, stats: { sessionCount, messageCount, totalInput, totalOutput, ... }, models, todos, prompts, ... }`

### GET /api/projects/{project}/sessions
All sessions for a project, from the harness's sessions index (or its JSONL files enriched from our database).
- `?sort=modified&order=desc` — sort by any index field (`modified`, `created`, `messageCount`, …); default `modified`, `desc`
→ `{ project, originalPath, sessions: [{ sessionId, firstPrompt, messageCount, created, modified, gitBranch, ..., displayName, chain }] }`

### GET /api/projects/{project}/tree
Browse a project's files. Reads the working tree from disk; a `ref` other than HEAD reads from git.
- `?path=src/lib` — directory or file inside the repo (default root)
- `?ref=HEAD` — branch, tag or commit
→ directory: `{ type: "tree", path, branch, entries: [...], lastCommit, readme }` · file: `{ type: "file", path, name, content? | binary? | image?, size, language, lastCommit }`

### GET /api/projects/{project}/visibility
Scrobble visibility for a project.
→ `{ projectId, visibility: public|unlisted|private, autoDetected, updatedAt }`

### POST /api/projects/{project}/visibility
← `{ visibility: "public" | "unlisted" | "private" }`
→ `{ success: true, visibility }`

### GET /api/projects/{project}/git
Git status for a project repo (cached 5 s). A tracked directory with no `.git` answers `vcs: false`, not an error.
→ `{ repoPath, branch, files: [{ status, file }], diffStat, diff, recentCommits, isDirty }`

### POST /api/projects/{project}/git
Commit changes in a project repo, then push unless our `git_auto_push` setting is `false`.
← `{ message: "Fix auth bug", addAll?: true, skipPush?: false }` — without `addAll`, only tracked files are staged (`git add -u`)
← `{ action: "push" }` — push only; rebases and retries when the remote is ahead, 409 on conflict
→ `{ success: true, commit: "abc123 Fix auth bug", pushed: true, pushError? }`

### DELETE /api/projects/{project}/git
Act on one file in a project repo.
← `{ file: "path/in/repo", action: "delete" | "gitignore" | "restore" }`
→ `{ success: true, action, file }`

### POST /api/projects/{project}/git/suggest
Generate a commit message from our diff using an LLM.
- Header: `x-vault-api-key: sk-...` (optional, decrypted BYOK key for a configured endpoint)
→ `{ message: "Fix login redirect on expired sessions", provider: "claude-max" }`
Provider fallback: configured endpoint (vault BYOK key) → Claude Max OAuth → settings API key (OpenAI) → Qwen 3 Coder mesh → Hermes 3 mesh

### GET /api/projects/{project}/agent
Last 20 agent actions dispatched for a project.
→ `{ actions: [...] }`

### POST /api/projects/{project}/agent
Dispatch an agent action against a project's repo.
← `{ action: "status" | "finish" | "blockers" | "nudge", message?: "commit message for finish", trigger?: "manual" }`
→ `{ ok: true, actionId, result }`; `nudge` spawns a harness in our background and answers `{ ok: true, actionId, status: "spawned", harness }`


## Dashboard & Analytics

### GET /api/dashboard
Aggregate dashboard metrics, served from a payload our worker keeps warm; `X-Computed-At` says how old it is.
- `?range=7d` — 1h, 3h, 6h, 12h, 24h, 7d, 14d, 28d, 90d, 180d, 365d, all (default `7d`)
→ `{ range, ingestLagMinutes, summary, modelBreakdown, dailyActivity, hourCounts, dayOfWeekCounts, dowHourHeatmap }`

### GET /api/tokens
Token usage analytics. Served from a payload our worker keeps warm; `X-Computed-At` says how old it is.
- `?range=7d` — 1h, 3h, 6h, 12h, 24h, 7d, 14d, 28d, 90d, 180d, 365d, all (default `all`); an unknown name is a 400 listing the valid ones
- `?project=<encoded-name>` — scope to one project; builds live for the range's window
- `?from=<ISO>&to=<ISO>` — an explicit window; always builds live, never served from the store
→ `{ modelBreakdown, harnessData, harnessModelBreakdown, harnessSessions, toolCalls, toolsByHarness, toolsByModel, blockTypes, dailyActivity, dailyByHarness, dailyModelTokens, totalInput, totalOutput, totalCacheRead, totalCacheWrite, totalTokens, totalInputCost, totalOutputCost, totalCacheReadCost, totalCacheWriteCost, totalCost }`

### GET /api/usage
Usage timeline or by-project breakdown, from per-minute usage rows.
- `?minutes=60` — time window (buckets per minute up to 24h, per hour up to 14d, per day beyond)
- `?view=projects` — group by project (default `timeline`)
→ Timeline array or project breakdown

### GET /api/usage/plan
Claude subscription plan and what this billing period would have cost at API rates. Read from `~/.claude/.credentials.json` and `~/.claude.json`.
→ `{ subscriptionType, rateLimitTier, hasExtraUsageEnabled, monthlyPlanCost, periodStart, periodEnd, periodCostUSD, periodInputTokens, periodOutputTokens, periodCacheReadTokens, periodCacheWriteTokens, dailyCost }`

### GET /api/usage/extra
The last extra-usage snapshot pushed to us, stamped with whether it still describes our current billing period. CORS-open (`OPTIONS` answers preflight) so a browser extension on claude.ai can push it.
→ `{ extraSpent, extraLimit, extraBalance, extraResetDate, extraUpdatedAt, resetAt, expired, expiredReason: null | "reset_passed" | "too_old" }`

### POST /api/usage/extra
Push an extra-usage snapshot; any field left out keeps its last value.
← `{ spent?, limit?, balance?, resetDate? }`
→ `{ ok: true }`

### GET /api/onboarding
What a first run needs, all local: each harness root ingest reads (core's detector — the same one Settings and `make doctor` use) with `found`, `readable`, `files` (one project level deep, capped; `truncated` says so), `newestMs`, `doc` (adapter doc under the schema package's docs/), and `sessions` / `lastMessageAt` from our database; our totals; and whether our worker is alive (an ingest heartbeat within 10 min; `payloadAt`, the freshest stored payload, is reported but proves only that a page was opened). The first-run wizard polls it every 6 s, Settings → Harnesses every 30 s. Takes no parameters.
→ `{ harnesses: [{ id, label, root, doc, start?, found, readable, files, newestMs, truncated, sessions, lastMessageAt }], sessions, projects, messages, lastIngestAt, payloadAt, workerAlive, checkedAt }`

### GET /api/reports/monthly
One calendar month of spend, itemised for an expense claim. Each line names its basis: `stated` (a provider's own figure), `priced` (tokens at our price ledger on the day spent), `measured` (sampled watts × hours × the node's $/kWh), `flat` (a configured monthly amount). Claude Code usage under a detected Claude subscription, and the market value of self-hosted models, are `memo` lines, never in the total. Amounts are USD; the report carries the one rate a renderer converts at, for the first currency in `display_currency` on the month's last day (ECB via Frankfurter, CoinGecko for crypto), and falls back to USD with a `fallbackReason` when no rate can be had. A closed month is filed when first built and served as filed afterwards.
- `month` — `YYYY-MM` (default: last month in `tz`)
- `tz` — IANA zone the month is read in (default: the server's)
- `format` — `json` (default), `csv` (one row per line, memo rows `counted=no`, a total, the rate) or `pdf`
- `rebuild=1` — build and file a closed month again
→ `{ month, timeZone, periodStart, periodEnd, closed, generatedAt, currency: { code, rate, rateDate, source, fallbackReason? }, lines: [{ category, item, detail, basis, usd }], memo: [{ item, detail, usd }], byCategory, byProject, byModel, totalUSD, notes }`; 400 on a bad month, zone or format, or a month not yet begun

### GET /api/training-export
Our sessions as supervised fine-tuning data: NDJSON, one line per session in our chat SFT shape `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":…},{"role":"assistant","content":…,"tool_calls"?:[{"id","type":"function","function":{"name","arguments"}}],"reasoning_content"?},{"role":"tool","tool_call_id","content"}]}` (OpenAI fine-tuning / TRL), as a download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`). Every string is redacted for secrets (API keys, tokens, JWTs, private keys, URL passwords, `password=`-style assignments), the username in home paths, and PII (emails, phones, cards, SSNs, public IPs): replaced by a `__TYPE_N__` token, never dropped. Calls and results are paired within a turn; system and sidechain lines are left out. Rendering rules and our JSON Schema for a line (`SFT_EXAMPLE_JSON_SCHEMA`): `packages/core/training-export.ts`.
- `project` — encoded project name or an alias of it (404 when neither)
- `model` — sessions with an assistant message on this model
- `harness` — `sessions.harness` (none means `claude-code`)
- `from`, `to` — session start, ISO date or instant; a bare `to` date covers that whole day
- `toolErrors` — `turn` (default: drop a turn whose tool result errored), `session` (drop its session) or `keep`
- `minTurns`, `maxTurns` — turns kept after tool-error filtering; a session outside is skipped
- `reasoning=1` — include reasoning as `reasoning_content` (off by default)
- `tools=0` — drop tool calls and results, keep the prose
- `metadata=1` — add `metadata: { session, project (display name), harness, models, startedAt, turns }`
- `toolResultMaxChars` — cut tool output past N characters with a `…[truncated N chars]` marker
- `limit` — stop after N examples
- `dryRun=1` — answer JSON instead of the file: `{ filters, stats: { sessionsScanned, examples, turns, messages, toolCalls, toolResults, turnsDroppedForToolErrors, skipped: { toolErrors, tooFewTurns, tooManyTurns, empty }, redactions: { <type>: n }, redactionsTotal }, sample, bytes }`
- `facets=1` — answer `{ harnesses, models }` seen in `project` (or everywhere), for a filter form
→ `application/x-ndjson` file `unfirehose-training-<project>-<date>.jsonl`; 400 on a filter that cannot mean anything

### GET /api/stats
Claude Code's own `~/.claude/stats-cache.json`, passed through. Takes no parameters.
→ Aggregate stats object

### GET /api/active-sessions
Currently active sessions.
- `?minutes=10` — activity window (default 10)
- `?sidechain=true|false|all` — subagent filter; `true` = only running subagents (Task-spawned), `false` = only top-level, `all` (default) = both
→ `{ sessions: [{ id, sessionUuid, displayName, gitBranch, isSidechain, delegatedFrom, harness, updatedAt, createdAt, projectName, projectDisplay, projectPath, messageCount, recentTokens, recentInput, recentOutput, recentCacheRead, recentCacheWrite, lastModel, reasoningCount, readableReasoningCount }], count }`

### GET /api/live
Server-sent events stream of live session activity.
→ SSE: `{ type: "sessions", sessions }` then `{ type: "entry", project, projectName, ... }` per new JSONL line

### GET /api/pricing
Our price book: every oracle's status, the sync register, prices that moved in the last 30 days, and a resolution + consensus report for every model in our database.
- `?model=claude-opus-5&at=2026-06-01` — how one model name resolves (candidates, each oracle's answer, agreement), optionally as of a past instant
- `?history=anthropic/claude-opus-5` — step series for one upstream id → `{ modelId, rows }`
- `?summary=1` — light form without per-model coverage
→ `{ oracles, register, recentChanges, changesByDay, pins, promos, selfHost, coverage, unpriced, disagreements, unpricedRecent }`

### POST /api/pricing
Force a sync from every price oracle (recorded as trigger `api`).
→ `{ results, catalog }`

### GET /api/metrics
Real-user web-vitals aggregates per page.
- `?days=7` — window (1–90)
→ `{ days, totalSamples, aggregates: [{ pathname, metrics: { [TTFB|FCP|LCP|INP|CLS]: { count, p50, p75, p95 } } }] }`

### POST /api/metrics
Record one web-vitals sample.
← `{ pathname, metric: "TTFB" | "FCP" | "LCP" | "INP" | "CLS", value, rating: "good" | "needs-improvement" | "poor", sessionId? }`
→ `{ ok: true }`

### GET /api/db/meta
Our SQLite database's size and shape: pragmas, page and file sizes, and per-table and per-index byte counts, largest first.
→ `{ pageSize, pageCount, freelistCount, cacheSize, journalMode, walCheckpoint, totalBytes, usedBytes, freeBytes, fileSize, totalBytesHuman, usedBytesHuman, freeBytesHuman, fileSizeHuman, tables: [...], indexes: [...] }`

### GET /api/db/health
What Settings → Database shows. Cheap: pragmas, one stat, and our worker's
newest daily size snapshot (`db_size_snapshots`); never a dbstat scan.
`growthPerWeekBytes` is the slope of live bytes (freelist left out) over up
to 28 days of snapshots, null until two days exist. `diskLevel` is `low`
under 10 GB free on the filesystem under our database, `critical` under 1 GB.
→ `{ path, pageSize, dbBytes, freelistBytes, walBytes, disk: { path, freeBytes, totalBytes } | null, diskLevel: "ok" | "low" | "critical" | "unknown", lowDiskBytes, dbstat, snapshot: { day, takenAt, dbBytes, freelistBytes, walBytes, method: "dbstat" | "pages", tables: [{ name, bytes, indexBytes, rows }] } | null, history: [{ day, dbBytes, liveBytes }], growthPerWeekBytes, cold: { blocks, rawBytes, storedBytes }, retention: { days, choices, minDays } }`

### POST /api/db/health
Take today's size snapshot now instead of waiting for our worker. Reads
every page through dbstat, so seconds on a large database.
← `{ action: "measure" }`
→ the GET body plus `measuredMs`

### GET /api/db/retention
Our retention window for content-block text. `days: null` (our default)
keeps every block's text hot. With a window, our worker moves text of
blocks older than it, compressed (brotli), into `content_blocks_cold`
while ingest is quiet; every reader gets it back byte for byte, and token,
cost and message counts never change (they live on `messages`).
→ `{ days, choices: [30, 90, 180, 365], minDays: 30, cold: { blocks, rawBytes, storedBytes } }`

### POST /api/db/retention
- `{ action: "estimate", days }` — dry run, changes nothing → `{ days, cutoff, blocks, rawBytes, estimatedColdBytes, estimatedSavedBytes, ratio, sampled, measuredMs }`
- `{ action: "set", days }` — save the window; `null` or `"off"` keeps everything → `{ days, cold }`
- `{ action: "thaw", days? }` — put one batch (5,000 blocks) of cold text back hot; with `days`, only blocks inside that window → `{ blocks, done, cold }`
- 400 for a window under 30 days or an unknown action


## Mesh / Permacomputer

### GET /api/mesh
All mesh node stats (SSH-connected machines), served from our worker's newest
`mesh_snapshots` row per node (sampled every 15 s). A node with no sample
inside 60 s is reported unreachable with when it was last heard from. Static
facts (CPU model, disks, uptime, OS, containers) come from a full probe run
behind the response at most every 5 min. Falls back to an inline SSH probe
only when no node has a fresh snapshot.
- `?live=1` — force the inline SSH probe of every node now (seconds, not milliseconds)
- `?host=cammy` — probe one node inline, no summary
- Headers: `X-Mesh-Source: snapshots|cache|live`, `X-Computed-At` (the oldest sample the answer rests on)
→ `{ nodes: [...], localHostname, summary }`

### GET /api/mesh/history
Time-series metrics for mesh nodes, peak-preserving downsampled.
- `?hours=24` — window
- `?hostname=cammy` — one node (default `all`)
- `?points=600` — target points after downsampling (50–5000)
- `?nodes=0` — drop the per-node breakdown from each point
→ `{ timeline: [{ timestamp, cpuPercent, memUsedGB, memTotalGB, gpuUtil, gpuMemUsedGB, ..., nodes? }], hostnames, hours, count, sampled, of }`

Energy hosts carry `grade` ('B' exact joules from RAPL+NVML counters over ≥95% of sampled time, 'C' integrated watts), `measuredCoverage` (0..1), `measuredKwh`, and `idleSource` ('measured' from vLLM empty-queue reports, or 'p10'). Ticket 4013.

### POST /api/mesh/history
Ingest snapshot from mesh nodes (append-only).
← `{ nodes: [...] }`
→ `{ ok: true, recorded }`

### GET /api/mesh/node
Deep probe of a single node.
- `?host=cammy` — required
→ CPU, memory, GPU, temps, processes, network, Docker, tmux, screen sessions; `{ hostname, reachable: false, error, probedAt }` when the probe fails

### GET /api/mesh/geoip
GeoIP of each mesh node's egress IP (cached; rate-limited to ip-api.com's 45/min).
→ `{ nodes: [{ hostname, ip, city, region, regionCode, country, countryCode, isp, org, as, lat, lon, timezone, error? }] }`

### GET /api/mesh/rates
Currency exchange rates for cost calculations (Frankfurter/ECB fiat + CoinGecko crypto). Off when our `mesh_currency_oracle` setting is `false`.
→ `{ fiat: {...}, crypto: {...}, source, updatedAt }`

### GET /api/inference/cache
Prefix-cache hit rate vLLM measured on each node and model over a window — what our token accounting cannot show, since a self-hosted model reports no cache tokens.
- `?hours=24` — window (max 90 days)
→ `{ hours, models: [{ hostname, model, windowHitRate, windowQueries, windowHits, lifetimeHitRate, lifetimeQueries, lifetimeHits, kvUsage, kvSizeTokens, prefixCachingEnabled, samples, lastSeen }] }`

### POST /api/inference/cache
Sample every mesh node's vLLM metrics now.
→ `{ nodes: [...] }`


## Boot & Harness Management

### POST /api/boot
Boot a harness session (Claude Code by default) in tmux on localhost or a mesh node, or in a container an integration that is on provides (see Integrations).
← `{ projectPath, host?: "localhost" | "<mesh node>" | "<integration host>", sessionId?, yolo?, prompt?, parentSessionUuid?, todoIds?: [...], projectName?, harness?: "claude", harnessKey?, model?, preferMultiplexer?: "tmux" | "screen", bootstrap?, sudoPassword?, repoUrl? }`
→ `{ success, tmuxSession, tmuxWindow, multiplexer, host, command }`

### POST /api/boot/finished
Called by an agent when it is done: sends `/exit` to its tmux window and marks the deployment completed.
← `{ tmuxSession, tmuxWindow? }` or `{ projectName }` or `{ todoId }`
→ `{ ok: true, exited: [...] }`

### GET /api/boot/mega
Status of every running deployment, checked against live tmux sessions.
→ `{ active, dead, allDone, deployments: [...] }`

### POST /api/boot/mega
Mega-boot: spawn one agent per project with open todos.
← `{ maxAgents?: 10 }`
→ `{ launched, total, results: [...] }`

### DELETE /api/boot/mega
Cull deployments whose todos are all done, and record dead ones.
→ `{ culled, dead, culledProjects, deadProjects }`

### GET /api/harness/models
Models a harness can run on a target, so dispatch picks a model rather than a harness default.
- `?harness=uncloseai` — required
- `?host=4090-ai.foxhop.net` — default localhost
- `?refresh=1` — skip our cache
→ `{ harness, host, models: [...], selectable, source: static|none|cache|local|ssh|error, error? }`

### POST /api/harness/verify
Install (optional) and verify a harness on localhost or a remote node.
← `{ host?, install?: "npm i -g ...", verify: "claude --version" }` — shell commands; `verify` is required
→ `{ success, version, steps: [{ step, ok, output }] }`

### GET /api/tmux/stream
SSE stream of tmux terminal output.
- no `session` — list sessions → `{ sessions, deployments }`
- `?session=mysession` — stream that session
- `?window=2` — one window
- `?windows=true` — list a session's windows → `{ windows }`
- `?host=cammy` — a mesh node over SSH

### POST /api/tmux/stream
Send keystrokes to a tmux session.
← `{ session, keys: "ls -la", host?, window? }` · `{ session, special: "Enter" }` (named keys: Enter, Escape, Tab, C-c, arrows, …) · `{ session, action: "resize", cols, rows }`
→ `{ ok: true, content? }`

### POST /api/tmux/new
Create a detached tmux session.
← `{ name, host?, command?: "zsh || bash", cwd? }`
→ `{ ok: true, name, host }`; 409 when the name exists

### POST /api/tmux/upload
Upload a file into a session's machine. `multipart/form-data` with `file`, `session` and optional `host` (a host an integration owns writes to `/tmp/input/` in its container; max 50 MB either way).
→ `{ ok: true, path, name }`

### GET /api/sessions/nickname
Every session nickname.
→ `{ [session_id]: { nickname, host, service_name, updated_at } }`

### POST /api/sessions/nickname
Upsert a nickname; fields left out keep their value.
← `{ session_id, nickname?, host?, service_name? }`
→ `{ ok: true }`

### DELETE /api/sessions/nickname
← `{ session_id }`
→ `{ ok: true }`


## Integrations

Optional products this dashboard can talk to, each off by default. While an integration is off it makes no requests, adds nothing to any page, and every route it owns answers 404 `{ error: "Not found", integration, detail }`; a `host` it owns on `/api/boot` or `/api/tmux/upload` gets the same 404.

Turn one on in Settings → Integrations, with `POST /api/integrations`, or for the whole process with `UNFIREHOSE_INTEGRATIONS=<id>[,<id>…]` in the environment (when set, the environment decides and the toggle is locked; `none` turns all off). The setting behind the toggle is `integration_<id>` = `"true"`.

| id | adds | routes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unsandbox` | unsandbox.com cloud containers: a node card and keys panel on /permacomputer, the /permacomputer/unsandbox page, container sessions under /tmux, a boot target on project pages (host `unsandbox`) | `/api/unsandbox`, `/api/unsandbox/shell`, `/api/unsandbox/sync` |

### GET /api/integrations
Every integration, and whether it is on.
→ `{ env: "UNFIREHOSE_INTEGRATIONS", integrations: [{ id, name, summary, hosts, href, enabled, source: "env" | "setting" | "default" }] }`

### POST /api/integrations
Turn one on or off.
← `{ id, enabled: true | false }`
→ `{ ok: true, id, enabled, source }`; 400 for an unknown id, 409 while `UNFIREHOSE_INTEGRATIONS` decides

### GET /api/unsandbox
Our unsandbox.com proxy (HMAC-signed with our stored keys).
- no `action` — key status → `{ connected, tier, rateLimit, maxSessions, expiresAt, expiresAtHuman, burst }`
- `?action=sessions` → `{ sessions: [...] }`
- `?action=services` → `{ services: [...] }`

### POST /api/unsandbox
Proxy one unsandbox action.
← `{ action: "test" }` · `{ action: "probe" }` (system probe inside a container)
← `{ action: "execute", language, code, network?: "zerotrust" | "semitrusted" }`
← `{ action: "session", image?, network? }` · `{ action: "kill-session", sessionId }` · `{ action: "session-exec", sessionId, command }`
← `{ action: "create-service", name?, ports, bootstrap, network? }` (`name` gets our key suffix; response adds `resolvedName`)
← `{ action: "destroy-service" | "service-info" | "service-logs" | "service-wake" | "service-redeploy", serviceId }`

### GET /api/unsandbox/shell
SSE stream of an unsandbox session's or service's shell output (bridged from its WebSocket). A sleeping service reports `{ type: "service_state", state }` and connects once it wakes.
- `?session_id=...` — required

### POST /api/unsandbox/shell
Send input to an unsandbox shell.
← `{ session_id, keys: "ls -la" }` · `{ session_id, special: "Enter" }` · `{ session_id, action: "resize", cols, rows }`
→ `{ ok: true }`

### HEAD /api/unsandbox/shell
Liveness check for our shell bridge.

### GET /api/unsandbox/sync
Unsandbox services with when each was last synced.
→ `{ services: [{ id, name, status, created_at, lastSync }] }`

### POST /api/unsandbox/sync
Pull harness JSONL (`~/.claude/projects`) back from unsandbox services so it can be ingested here. Delta-aware: only files changed since our last sync travel.
← `{ serviceId: "unsb-service-..." }` or `{ all: true }` (every running service)
→ `{ results: [...] }`


## Scrobble (Social Feed)

### GET /api/scrobble/payload
Full scrobble payload for publishing to the network, precomputed by our worker; `X-Computed-At` says how old it is.
→ `{ $schema, generatedAt, handle, lifetime, streaks, badges, activity, timeSeries, models, tools, projects }`

### GET /api/scrobble/preview
What a scrobble would publish, per project, with visibility.
→ `{ projects: [{ name, displayName, visibility, autoDetected, sessionCount, messageCount, totalInput, totalOutput }], included: [...], excluded: [...] }`


## Schema & Documentation

### GET /api/schema
Browse our unfirehose/1.0 schema docs (`packages/schema/docs`).
- `?file=README.md` or `?file=harnesses/claude-code.md` — read one `.md` file
→ `{ files: [{ path, label, group }] }` or `{ file, content }`


## Settings & Configuration

### GET /api/settings
All settings as key-value pairs.
→ `{ theme_accent_color, unfirehose_plan, ..., _system_username }`

### POST /api/settings
Set, delete, or bulk-set settings.
← `{ action: "set", key: "theme_accent_color", value: "#d40000" }`
← `{ action: "delete", key: "theme_accent_color" }`
← `{ action: "bulk_set", settings: { key: value, ... } }`
→ `{ ok: true, ... }`

### DELETE /api/settings
Delete one setting.
← `{ key: "theme_accent_color" }`
→ `{ ok: true }`

### GET /api/lan
This machine's IPv4 addresses a phone on the same network could open, for the QR in Settings → Phone. From `os.networkInterfaces()`, skipping loopback, link-local (169.254/16), IPv6, and container or VM bridges (`docker0`, `br-*`, `veth*`, `virbr*`, …); each kept address is `lan` (a private range), `vpn` (a tunnel interface or 100.64/10) or `public`, in that order. `url` uses the port this request arrived on; `listening` is a local TCP probe of `address:port`. The probe never leaves this machine and cannot see a firewall in front of the phone. Takes no parameters.
`bind` says where our server listens. It listens on 127.0.0.1 unless opted in: `npm run dev` / `npm run start` (so `make dev`, `make demo`, the systemd unit) go through `apps/web/scripts/serve.mjs`, which passes `next -H` from, in order, `UNFIREHOSE_HOST` (decides alone; `override`), `$UNFIREHOSE_DIR/web-bind.json` `{"lan": true}` → `0.0.0.0` (`saved`, written by POST below), else `127.0.0.1`. `running` is the host this server was started on (null when started some other way), `next` what a restart would pick, `restartNeeded` when they differ, `container` inside our Docker image (where compose's port mapping decides). There is no login on this dashboard: anyone who can open the URL sees everything.
→ `{ hostname, port, addresses: [{ address, iface, kind, url, listening }], skipped: [{ address, iface, reason }], bind: { running, runningLan, saved: { lan, setAt }, next: { host, lan, source: "env"|"settings"|"default" }, override, file, restartNeeded, container }, checkedAt }`

### POST /api/lan
Save whether our dashboard listens on the network from its next start (the bind is fixed when the server starts: `make dev` again, or `make service-restart`). Writes `$UNFIREHOSE_DIR/web-bind.json` (0600). Opening needs `understood: true`: anyone on the network can read every session, push commits and type into tmux, with no login. Refused cross-site (`Sec-Fetch-Site` other than same-origin, or a foreign `Origin`) with 403; with 409 while `UNFIREHOSE_HOST` is set or inside a container.
← `{ lan: true, understood: true }` or `{ lan: false }`
→ `{ ok: true, bind: { …as GET } }`

### GET /api/llm/providers
Discover available LLM providers (auto-detected + mesh).
→ `{ providers: [{ id, name, source, type, model, ready, detail }] }`


## Alerts

### GET /api/alerts
Usage alerts, and credential alerts: `alert_type: "secret_exposed"` (`metric: "secret"`, `window_minutes: 0`, `actual_value` = times seen in that session) is raised at ingest when a tool call or tool result in a session newer than `secret_alerts_since` carries a credential. Its `details` name the kinds, where (`call` | `result`, tool), session, project and line time; never the value.
- `?limit=20&offset=0` — recent alerts (max 200) → array
- `?paginate=1` — wrap as `{ alerts: [...], total, limit, offset }`
- `?filter=unacknowledged` — open alerts only
- `?filter=thresholds` — alert threshold rules
- `?filter=daily&days=14` — alert counts per day (1–365)

### POST /api/alerts
Manage alerts and thresholds.
← `{ action: "acknowledge", id: 123 }` · `{ action: "acknowledge_all" }`
← `{ action: "clear", scope?: "acknowledged" | "all" }` — delete what has been seen (default) or everything
← `{ action: "update_threshold", id, value, enabled? }` — open alerts under the old value are acknowledged
← `{ action: "calibrate", days?: 7, factor?: 1.5 }` — reset thresholds from recent usage
→ `{ ok: true, ... }`

### GET /api/alerts/delivery
Alert delivery rules (Settings → Alerts): which alerts go to a webhook, ntfy, Slack or Discord. `match.metric: "secret"` picks credential alerts only; `match.project` matches a project's encoded or display name. Counts are the last 24 h of real (non-test) attempts: `failed_24h` gave up, `dropped_24h` went over the hourly cap. Our worker sends each new alert once per rule, retries with backoff (30 s, 2 min, 8 min, 32 min; 5 attempts; 4xx other than 408/425/429 fails at once) and holds each rule to `rate_limit_per_hour` (over it: `rate_limited`, not sent). Secrets come back masked, never whole.
- `?limit=50` — recent delivery attempts (max 500)
→ `{ rules: [{ id, name, enabled, destination, config, match: { metric, window, project }, rate_limit_per_hour, secrets: { field: "••••abcd" | null }, last, sent_24h, failed_24h, dropped_24h, last_dropped_at }], deliveries: [{ alert_id, rule_id, is_test, status, http_status, error, attempts, next_retry_at, delivered_at }], destinations, secretFields, metrics }`

### POST /api/alerts/delivery
Create a rule. It delivers alerts raised from now on, never the backlog.
← `{ name?, destination: "webhook" | "ntfy" | "slack" | "discord", enabled?: true, config?, secrets?, match?: { metric?, window?, project? }, rate_limit_per_hour?: 10 }`
- webhook: `config: { url }` (http or https; localhost and LAN allowed), `secrets: { hmacSecret? }` → POST JSON `{ event: "alert.triggered" | "alert.test", version: 1, title, message, severity, path, alert }` with `X-Unfirehose-Timestamp` and, when a secret is set, `X-Unfirehose-Signature: sha256=HMAC_SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + body)`
- ntfy: `config: { server: "https://ntfy.sh", topic }`, `secrets: { token? }` → body is the message; `Title`, `Priority` (3/4/5), `Tags` headers
- slack, discord: `secrets: { webhookUrl }` (https)
→ 201 `{ ok: true, rule }` · 400 `{ error, errors: { field: reason } }`

### GET /api/alerts/delivery/{id}
One rule (secrets masked) and its last 50 attempts.
→ `{ rule, deliveries }`

### PATCH /api/alerts/delivery/{id}
Change a rule. Any field of POST but `destination`. A secret left out or `""` keeps what is stored; `null` clears it. Re-enabling starts from now.
→ `{ ok: true, rule }` · 400 `{ errors }` · 404

### DELETE /api/alerts/delivery/{id}
Remove a rule, its attempts and its stored secrets.
→ `{ ok: true }` · 404

### POST /api/alerts/delivery/{id}/test
Send one synthetic alert through the same build, sign and send path, once, no retry. Works on a disabled rule; recorded as a test attempt; never counts against the rate limit.
→ `{ ok, status: 204 | null, error: string | null }`

### GET /api/alerts/{id}
One alert with what happened inside its window: per-project and per-model usage and cost, active sessions, reasoning blocks, timeline, user prompts.
A credential alert answers `{ alert, secret: { kinds, location, tool, session, project, projectDisplay, harness, seenAt, blockId, toolUseId }, words: { title, message, where, kinds, sessionPath } }` instead.
→ `{ alert, window: { start, end, duration_minutes }, projectBreakdown, modelBreakdown, activeSessions, reasoningBlocks, timeline, userPrompts, totals, stats }`

### GET /api/rate-limits
Refusals — every way a provider declined a call (throttles, quota, overloaded, 5xx, model gone), from harness-reported records and scanned output.
- `?minutes=60` — window (`minutes=0` lifetime; `days=N` still accepted, default 30 days)
- `?target=inference|service|web|all` — default `inference`
- `?kind=all|throttles|<kind>` — default `all`; `throttles` = rate_limit, concurrency, quota, overloaded
- `?limit=100` — recent rows (max 500)
→ `{ days, minutes, target, kind, total, targets, kinds, byProvider, byUpstream, byDay, recent, now, attribution }` — every row carries `http_status`

### POST /api/rate-limits
← `{ fromScratch: true, drain: true, batch?: 5000 }` rescan history with current rules (`drain` runs batches to the newest block); `{ backfillReported: true }` rebuild harness-reported rows from JSONL on disk

### GET /api/rate-limits/status
Vendor status pages as our worker last polled them (language-model vendors only; incident feeds, robots.txt honoured).
- `?history=<targetId>&hours=24` → `{ target, hours, history: [{ timestamp, indicator, description, http_status, latency_ms }] }`
→ `{ current: [{ id, name, url, feed, since, poll: { indicator: none|minor|major|unknown|unreachable|blocked_by_robots, description, incidents: [...] } }] }`

### POST /api/rate-limits/status
← `{ action: "add", target: { id: "mistral", name: "Mistral", feed: "https://status.mistral.ai/history.atom" } }` · a vendor with no status page: `{ action: "add", target: { id, name, kind: "http-probe", feed: "https://api.example/v1/models", expect: [200] } }`
← `{ action: "remove", id: "x-ai" }` · `{ action: "poll" }` polls every target now


## Actions

### GET /api/actions
Agent action ledger — every tool call that touched the filesystem, git or the network, newest first, classified from ingested content blocks for every harness (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, pi, hermes tool names). Secrets are redacted from what it returns.
- `?project=<encoded name or alias>` · `?session=<uuid>` · `?harness=claude-code` · `?tool=Bash`
- `?from=2026-10-01&to=2026-10-23` — ISO instants or dates, both inclusive
- `?kind=fs-read|fs-write|git|network|shell`
- `?flag=any|destructive|force-push|force-with-lease|secrets-in-diff|secret-in-command|sudo|curl-pipe-shell|secret-in-output`
- network: curl, ssh and the like; package installs (npm i/ci/exec, pnpm, yarn, bun, pip, python -m pip, pipx, uv/uvx, poetry, conda, cargo, go get, gem, bundle, composer, dotnet, deno, apt, brew…); every MCP tool (`mcp__*`). A credential handed to a network or MCP tool is `secret-in-command`; one in a tool's output is `secret-in-output`.
- `?path=<substring>` (paths, URLs, hosts) · `?command=<substring>`
- `?limit=100` (max 500) · `?cursor=<nextCursor>` keyset paging · `?format=csv` downloads up to 10 000 matching rows
→ `{ rows: [{ id, timestamp, kind, tool, harness, paths, command, flags, reasons, projectName, projectDisplayName, sessionUuid, toolUseId }], nextCursor, total, kinds, flags, flaggedRows, status: { rows, backfillRemaining, headLag, rulesVersion, secrets: { sightings, alerted, since } } }`

### POST /api/actions
← `{ rebuild: true }` empties our ledger and re-classifies from content blocks (one window now, our worker fills history in the background); `{}` runs one window of catch-up
→ `{ ok, rebuilt, rows, backfillRemaining, headLag, rulesVersion, secrets, done }`


## Triage

### GET /api/triage
Triage overview: totals, projects with stale sessions and open todos, and the stale sessions themselves.
- `?project=...` — one project
- `?days=7` — staleness threshold
- `?limit=25` — max projects (max 50)
→ `{ thresholdDays, totals: { activeSessions, closedSessions, openTodos, closedTodos, staleSessions, staleTodos }, projects: [...], sessions: [...] }`

### POST /api/triage
Execute triage actions in one transaction.
← `{ actions: [{ action: "close_project_sessions", project, olderThanDays }, { action: "close_sessions", sessionUuids: [...] }, { action: "obsolete_todos", todoIds: [...] }, { action: "keep_todos", todoIds: [...] }] }`
→ `{ ok: true, results: [...] }`

### GET /api/sessions/stale
Sessions inactive past a threshold, with their open todo counts — candidates for closing.
- `?days=7` — inactivity threshold
- `?project=...`
- `?status=active` — session status to consider
- `?limit=50` — max 200
→ `{ thresholdDays, summary: { total, active, closed, stale }, sessions: [{ id, sessionUuid, displayName, firstPrompt, gitBranch, status, cliVersion, createdAt, updatedAt, lastMessageAt, inactiveDays, projectName, projectDisplay, messageCount, pendingTodos, totalTodos }] }`

### PATCH /api/sessions/close
Close sessions (kept for history, never deleted) and by default obsolete the todos they left open.
← `{ sessionUuids: [...] }` or `{ project, olderThanDays: 14 }` (max 500), plus `obsoleteTodos?: true`, `reason?`
→ `{ ok: true, closedSessions, obsoletedTodos, reason }`


## Providence (answer cache)

### GET /api/providence
Recorded question/answer provenance rows, newest first.
- `?uri=...&root=...&git=...&model_id=...&backend=...&node_id=...` — each narrows one column
- `?limit=50` — max 200
→ `{ total, rows: [...] }`

### POST /api/providence
Record an answer with its provenance. A repeat of the same cache key counts a hit instead of inserting.
← `{ document_root, document_uri, question_text, answer_text, model_id?, model_revision?, quantization?, conversation_hash?, seed?, ... }` (every other `providence_cache` column is optional)
→ `{ id, cache_key, hit }` (201 when new)

### DELETE /api/providence
- `?id=123` or `?uri=...`
→ `{ deleted }`

### GET /api/providence/lookup
Look up a cached answer by its key inputs; a different model, quantization or prompt is a different entry.
- `?q=<question>` — required
- `?root=<merkle or git root>` or `?git=<commit>` — one required
- `?model_id=&model_revision=&quantization=&conversation_hash=&seed=` — optional key inputs
→ `{ hit: false, cache_key, document_root, question_hash }` or `{ hit: true, answer, ...provenance, hit_count }`


## Ingest

### GET /api/ingest
Database row counts.
→ `{ projects, sessions, messages, contentBlocks, thinkingBlocks, totalTokensStored, alerts }`

### POST /api/ingest
Start an on-demand ingest pass over every harness log, in a detached worker process. Answers 202 at once; one pass at a time.
→ `{ started: true, pid, startedAt }` or `{ started: false, alreadyRunning: true, pid, startedAt }`

## Maintenance

### POST /api/pii-backfill
Scan and redact PII from stored conversation data.
→ `{ ok, blocksScanned, blocksModified, sessionsModified, piiReplacementsAdded }`

### GET /api/ssh-config
Parse and list SSH config hosts and keys.
→ `{ hosts: [...], keys: [...], hash }`

### POST /api/ssh-config
Add or update an SSH config entry. Pass the `hash` you loaded; a config changed on disk since then is a 409.
← `{ name, hostname, port?, user?, identityFile?, forwardAgent?, originalName?, hash? }` — `originalName` renames an existing block
→ `{ ok: true, host, hash }`

### DELETE /api/ssh-config
← `{ name, hash? }`
→ `{ ok: true, hash }`

### GET /api/apmonitor
APMonitor statefiles from localhost and every mesh node.
- `?host=...` — one host only (returns its state directly)
- `?path=...` — override our statefile path (else our `apmonitor_statefile` setting)
→ `{ nodes: [...], summary: { totalResources, up, down, nodesPolled, nodesWithData } }`

### POST /api/apmonitor
Webhook receiver for APMonitor outage/recovery notifications (point its `outage_webhooks` here). Keeps the last 1000 raw payloads.
→ `{ ok: true, received_at }`


## Agent Workflow Examples

### Start-of-session orientation
```bash
curl -s localhost:3000/api/todos/summary | python3 -m json.tool
curl -s "localhost:3000/api/todos/pending?project=-home-fox-git-myapp&limit=10"
curl -s "localhost:3000/api/projects/activity?days=7"
```

### Search conversation history
```bash
curl -s "localhost:3000/api/logs?search=auth+error&types=assistant&from=2026-03-01&limit=50"
curl -s "localhost:3000/api/logs?search=architecture&has_thinking=true&limit=100"
```

### Extract training data (thinking traces)
```bash
# Messages carrying reasoning for a project (previews; replay a session for full text)
curl -s "localhost:3000/api/logs?project=-home-fox-git-myapp&has_thinking=true&limit=500"

# Full session replay, thinking blocks included
curl -s "localhost:3000/api/sessions/SESSION_ID?project=-home-fox-git-myapp&types=user,assistant"

# Scrobble payload — structured activity + model usage data
curl -s localhost:3000/api/scrobble/payload
```

### Todo management
```bash
# Create via API
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/todos -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"content":"Fix auth","source":"manual"}'

# Bulk complete
curl -X PATCH localhost:3000/api/todos/bulk -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"ids":[1,2,3],"status":"completed"}'

# Quick wins
curl -s "localhost:3000/api/todos/pending?quick=true&limit=20"
```

### Create todos via JSONL (no API needed)

Any agent can create todos by writing a JSONL session file. The ingest scanner
extracts `TaskCreate` tool_use blocks automatically — no HTTP calls required.

Write a `.jsonl` file to your session directory (e.g. `~/.claude/projects/<project>/*.jsonl`).
The scanner picks it up on next ingest and creates the todo in the database.

**Minimal JSONL for a todo** (3 lines):
```jsonl
{"type":"system","timestamp":"2026-03-11T16:00:00Z","sessionId":"SESSION_UUID","subtype":"init","message":{"role":"system","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Todo session"}]}}
{"type":"user","timestamp":"2026-03-11T16:00:01Z","sessionId":"SESSION_UUID","uuid":"USER_UUID","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Schedule work"}]}}
{"type":"assistant","timestamp":"2026-03-11T16:00:02Z","sessionId":"SESSION_UUID","uuid":"ASST_UUID","parentUuid":"USER_UUID","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Creating todo."},{"type":"tool_use","id":"tc-unique-id","name":"TaskCreate","input":{"subject":"The task title","description":"Detailed description of the work to be done.","status":"pending"}}],"model":"any-model"}}
```

**Supported tool_use names for todos:**
- `TaskCreate` — creates a new todo (`input.subject` = title, `input.description` = body)
- `TaskUpdate` — updates status (`input.taskId` = external ID, `input.status` = new status)
- `TodoWrite` — legacy batch format (`input.todos` = array of `{content, status, activeForm}`)

**Key behaviors:**
- Todos are keyed by `(project, external_id, source)` — duplicates are upserted, not duplicated
- Terminal statuses (`completed`, `obsolete`, `deleted`) are sticky — re-ingest won't reopen them
- The `source` field defaults to `"claude"` — set it in the todo to distinguish agent origins
- Session directory is determined by the project path encoded as a slug (slashes/dots → hyphens)

### Git operations from agents
```bash
# Check repo status
curl -s "localhost:3000/api/projects/-home-fox-git-myapp/git"

# Generate commit message (uses LLM fallback chain)
curl -X POST "localhost:3000/api/projects/-home-fox-git-myapp/git/suggest"

# Commit and push
curl -X POST "localhost:3000/api/projects/-home-fox-git-myapp/git" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"message":"Fix auth redirect","addAll":true}'
```

### Infrastructure monitoring
```bash
# All mesh nodes
curl -s localhost:3000/api/mesh

# 24h time-series for a node
curl -s "localhost:3000/api/mesh/history?hours=24&hostname=cammy"

# Deep probe
curl -s "localhost:3000/api/mesh/node?host=cammy"
```
